title: What to do after a road accident
summary: First your safety and any injured person, then evidence. Call 112 or 108 right away if anyone is hurt. Do not sign or settle anything on the spot.
steps: Move yourself to a safe place if you can. Switch off the engine
If anyone is badly hurt, call 108 for an ambulance or 112. Do not move a person with a neck or back injury unless there is fire or danger
Take photos of the vehicles, road and injuries. Note the vehicle number and witnesses
Tell the platform through the app so the accident is on record
Keep all hospital bills and papers. They are needed for any insurance claim
Do not sign blank papers or settle money on the spot

title: Safe riding and driving habits
summary: Most gig-worker injuries happen while rushing for a delivery or ride. A helmet, no phone in hand, and a slow start to wet roads prevent most serious injuries.
steps: Always wear a good helmet with the strap fastened
Never hold the phone while riding. Pull over to check orders
A late delivery is better than a crash. Do not speed to beat a timer
Check brakes, tyres and lights before a long shift
Take a break every 2 to 3 hours. Tired riders crash more

title: Working night shifts safely
summary: Night work has higher risks from poor visibility, fatigue and theft. Share your location with someone you trust, plan your route, and do not take risks for a single order.
steps: Share your live location with a family member or friend
Prefer main, well-lit roads even if the route is longer
Keep your phone charged and a power bank with you
If a pick-up or drop looks unsafe, you can decline or cancel and report it in the app
Keep little cash and keep your phone out of sight at traffic stops

title: Working in extreme heat
summary: Heat stroke can be deadly. Drink water often, rest in shade in the hottest hours, and know the warning signs.
steps: Drink water or ORS every 20 to 30 minutes, even if you are not thirsty
Rest in shade during 12 noon to 4 pm if you can
Cover your head and wear light cotton clothes
Warning signs: dizziness, headache, no sweat, confusion, very hot skin. Move to shade, cool the body with wet cloth, give water if awake, and call 108
Do not keep working if you feel unwell

title: Working in rain and floods
summary: Wet roads, waterlogging and open drains are serious dangers. Slow down, avoid flooded roads and keep electrical items away from water.
steps: Do not drive through flooded roads. You cannot see open drains or potholes
Brake early and gently on wet roads. Keep a larger gap
Wrap your phone and bag in plastic
Stay away from fallen wires and standing water near poles
During lightning, shelter in a building, not under a tree

title: Scams: fake calls, OTP and payment fraud
summary: Fraudsters pretend to be the platform, a bank or a customer. Never share an OTP, PIN or card details with anyone. Real support never asks for them. Report fast on 1930.
steps: Never share your OTP, UPI PIN, card number or app password with anyone, even if they say they are the platform or bank
Do not click links or install apps sent by unknown people
A customer who asks you to scan a QR code or approve a request to 'receive' money is a scam. You do not need to approve anything to receive money
Do not pay a 'KYC fee' or 'ID activation fee' to a stranger
If you lose money, call 1930 immediately and report at cybercrime.gov.in. Tell your bank too. Speed matters

title: Angry or abusive customer
summary: Your safety comes before any rating or order. Stay calm, do not argue, step away and report it in the app. If you feel threatened, leave and call 112.
steps: Stay calm. Do not argue or touch the customer
Move away to a public place. Your safety comes first
If you feel threatened, call 112
Report the incident in the app straight away and take screenshots of chats and the order
If a false complaint or bad rating leads to a penalty, ask for a review in writing and keep proof. We can help draft the complaint

title: Safety for women workers
summary: If you feel unsafe or are harassed, you are not at fault. Move to a safe public place, share your location, and call 181 or 112. You can decline an order or ride that feels unsafe.
steps: Move to a crowded, lit place and away from the person
Call 181 (women helpline) or 112. You do not have to be sure it is a crime to call
Share your live location with someone you trust
Report in the app and keep screenshots and call logs
It is your right to cancel an order or ride that feels unsafe

title: If the police stop you
summary: Stay calm and polite. Keep your documents ready in DigiLocker or mParivahan. Fines should be official e-challans or receipts. If you are detained, you have the right to inform someone and to ask the reason.
steps: Stay calm and polite. Show your licence, RC and insurance. Digital copies on DigiLocker or mParivahan are valid
Ask for an official e-challan or a receipt for any fine. Do not pay cash without a receipt
If you are taken to a police station, ask the reason and tell a family member or friend. Ask for free legal aid on 15100 if you need it
Never sign a blank or unread paper
